title: Three Lathes in a Berlin Backyard: How Siemens & Halske Began
conflicts: Loan: Werner Siemens's memoir and the NDB/ADB say 6,000 thalers from cousin Georg Siemens for a six-year profit share; a britishtelephones.com page excerpting the Siemens website says 6,842 thalers start-up capital. The story uses the founder's 6,000 and the page is not cited. Founding date: 1 October 1847 (agreement; Siemens Historical Institute, NDB) vs 12 October 1847 (workshop opened; memoir, NDB); the story gives both. When Halske met Siemens: NDB says 1845, siemens.com early 1847; the story dates neither. ADB says Halske left the firm in 1848, NDB and siemens.com say 1867; irrelevant to the story.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's 'mixed' to 'bootstrapped': a family loan for a profit share, and Siemens wrote the firm then grew without outside capital. The memoir is the 1893 Coupland translation read in full on the Internet Archive (djvu text). The story runs from the October 1847 opening through the 1848 revolution and the Frankfurt line to his June 1849 discharge, all one founding decision that he took in two steps.
